independent.summary: PUT /relationship-types/:id has no exact-name check, so the new Settings screen's Rename can silently create two types with the same name in one workspace — exactly the `owns`/`Owns` drift the vocabulary exists to prevent. POST refuses it with 409 and `routes/entityTypes.js` does the same clash check on its PUT (entityTypes.js:411), but this route only builds `update` and calls findOneAndUpdate. The diff's own docs now claim the opposite (`docs/api.md`: PUT applies the "same checks as POST"), `client/src/api/relationshipTypes.js` and `RelationshipTypeSettings.vue` document a cross-scope 409 as "the only thing that explains a refused rename", and `RelationshipTypeSettings.test.js` pins the refused-rename UI against a stubbed 409 the server can never send — so the one UI path that would surface the duplicate is dead code. Failure: rename "Owns" to "owned by" when a member-scoped "owned by" already exists → 200, the suggestion list now offers the same word twice from two rows, and the next rename of either is indistinguishable.

triageGrades.reason: The change gates the new settings group on `canWrite`, maps 401/403 to user-facing messages, and the server tests assert cross-tenant 404s on PUT/DELETE, so permissions are genuinely touched.
No credentials, tokens, env secrets or auth material appear anywhere in the diff.
Nothing in the diff involves billing, pricing, quotas or paid API usage.
The diff adds `deleteRelationshipType` plus an armed two-click Remove in the settings rows, i.e. a new data-deleting path.

The HTTP contract itself changes — POST/PUT now read `scope` (documented in docs/api.md) and a new client module calls four endpoints — so the API-surface category is touched, even if the calls are to this app's own server.
No version bumps, deploy/config changes or migrations; pre-existing rows just keep the model's `member` default.
